summary: @servicetitan/link-item preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute a 727KB obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases (v1.3.13) into a temp directory, chmod +x's the binary, and invokes it to execute a sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727KB heavily obfuscated Bun script using string-array rotation, hex-named identifiers, and a large numeric/string constant pool. The advertised functionality of the package is a small React link-item UI component (dist/ is ~4KB with a 104-byte index.js entry), which has no need for an alternate language runtime or a 727KB companion script. Fetching Bun from its official releases to run the package's own shipped code is not itself the dropper mechanism, but the shipped code here is a purpose-mismatched, install-time-executed obfuscated payload of the shape used by stealers/backdoors, and the @servicetitan scope-and-name framing is inconsistent with the shipped contents. Installing this package on default `npm install` causes the obfuscated payload to execute under a newly downloaded runtime on the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
